sentences.text: Court No. - 12

Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 2622 of 2023
Applicant :- Shaswat Sawarkar Singh

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. Prin.Secy.Deptt. Of Home And Ano
Counsel for Applicant :- Ajay Pratap Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
Sri Surendra Kumar Mishra, Advocate has put in appearance on behalf of the opposite party no.2 by
filing vakalatnama, the same is taken on record.

Heard Sri Ajay Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Surendra Kumar Mishra, learned
counsel for the opposite party no.2 and learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.
The instant application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant, namely, Shaswat
Sawarkar Singh with a prayer to quash the proceedings of Cis No.738 of 2023, "State Vs. Shaswat
Sawarkar Singh" arising out of F.I.R. No.0636 of 2022, under Sections 376, 392, 328, 323, 506
I.P.C., Police Station Kotwali Nagar, District Gonda as well as to quash the charge sheet dated
04.11.2022 filed on 14.12.2022 and summoning order dated 10.01.2023 passed in the aforesaid case.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that it is a case of false implication and infact the victim was having cordial relations with the applicant and the sexual relations between them have been established by free consent given by the prosecutrix/alleged victim.

While referring to the extract of whatsapp chat placed from page no.101 to 138, it is vehemently submitted that the prosecutrix/victim was a consenting party and it is only on account of her free consent, the sexual relations were established between them and since the prosecutrix was major, offence of rape could not be inferred from the facts and circumstances of the case.

It is also submitted that the relations between the applicant and the victim become strained and in this backdrop the first information report has been lodged by the victim on false and concocted facts and the statements of the prosecutirx recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. are also the result of biasness as the marriage of the applicant has been solemnized on 30.05.2022.
It is also submitted that the allegations of the prosecutrix are not supported by any medical evidence as the prosecutrix has refused to undergo for internal medical examination.

Learned counsel for the applicant has also relied on the law laid down in Pramod Suryabhan Pawar Vs. State of Maharashtra and Another; (2019) 9 SCC 608 in support of his contention that since the prosecutrix/victim was a consenting party, the offence of rape could not be attracted and, thus,
proceedings of the case pending before the trial court is nothing but an abuse of process of law and the same be quashed.

sentences.text: It is also submitted that during the course of investigation, the applicant was granted interim protection from arrest till the submission of report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. and the applicant has co-operated in the investigation but the Investigating Officer appears to have submitted the charge sheet without there being any material available in support of the allegation.
Learned A.G.A. on the other hand submitted that the applicant is accused of committing heinous offence, as such, he is not entitled for any relief.

Sri Surendra Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 has vehemently submitted that the applicant at first had committed rape on the victim after administering some noxious drink and thereafter had filmed an obscene video of her and on the pretext of making it viral, has committed rape on several occasions and the applicant has also withdrawn some money from the ATM card of the prosecutrix and had also taken her jewellery and keeping in view the manner in which the offence has been committed, the applicant is not entitled for any relief.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that in the first information report, which has been lodged by the victim herself on 17.09.2022 at Police Station Kotwali Nagar, District Gonda, specific allegations of commission of rape after administering some noxious substance in a drink has been levelled and the incident is shown to have occurred in the month of March, 2022.
It is also alleged that the applicant has also filmed an obscene video and it was subsequently on the basis of this obscene video, the rape on various occasions have been committed by the applicant.
Allegations of withdrawing money from the ATM card of the prosecutrix and snatching her jewellery and also of physical assault given by the applicant to the prosecutx have been levelled.
The allegations have been supported by the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.

Much emphasis has been given by the learned counsel for the applicant on the whatsapp chat, extract of which has been placed on record,
as in order to project that the relations of sexual relationship between the applicant and the victim were of consensual nature and the consent was free and was not obtained by any coercive means.

The sending of whatsapp message relied on by the applicant has not been admitted by the learned counsel representing the victim to be sent by the prosecutrix/victim, thus, in the considered opinion of this Court, the sending of whatsapp message relied on by the applicant is a debatable/disputable Shaswat Sawarkar Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. ... on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101484007/
2 issue which could only be proved during the course of trial and only on the basis of these whatsapp messages, the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. could not be doubted.

sentences.text: Having regard to the law relied by learned counsel for the applicant in the case of Pramod Suryabhan Pawar (Supra), suffice is to say that every criminal case is having its own facts and tenor and no state jacket formula could be adopted for measuring the gravity of each and every criminal case with a common yard stick.

In the considered opinion of this Court, the submissions which have been raised before this Court in order to negate the prosecution story, is not sufficient for the quashment of the proceedings pending before the court below.

Thus, having regard to the settled parameters for quashing of criminal proceedings as highlighted by Hon'ble Supreme Court in R.P. Kapur Vs. State of Punjab, AIR 1960 SC 866, State of Haryana Vs.
Bhajan Lal, 1992 SCC (Cr.) 426, Parabhatbhai Ahir & others Vs. State of Gujarat AIR 207 SC 4843 and Neeharika Infra Structure Pvt. Limited Vs. State of Maharashtra Criminal Appeal No. 330 of 2021, decided on 13.04.2021, I do not find any good ground on the basis of which criminal proceedings pending before the trial court against the applicant may be quashed.
Thus, in the considered opinion of this Court, no illegality appears to have been made either in submission of charge sheet or in taking of cognizance by the trial court or in issuance of process.
Thus, the application moved by the applicant under Section 482 Cr.P.C. appears to be devoid of merits and the same is accordingly dismissed.
